biography.plain_text: Gary Campbell Comer turned a sailing-equipment catalogue into Lands' End, a major American clothing retailer. His earlier career as an advertising copywriter helped shape its detailed product descriptions. From its Wisconsin base, the company expanded internationally, and Comer remained its controlling shareholder until the business was sold to Sears in 2002.

long_biography.plain_text:
Gary Campbell Comer, the founder of Lands' End, learned to sail after joining a Chicago Park District boat-shop programme. Local sailors taught him in exchange for sanding and scrubbing their boats. He later won North American Star Class championships and a Pan American Games bronze medal. A Northwest Passage journey prompted him to investigate climate change; he funded fellowships for scientists studying abrupt shifts in the climate.

Comer directed substantial support towards the South Side neighbourhood where he grew up. His gifts helped establish the Gary Comer Youth Center beside his former elementary school. With his wife Frances, he supported the creation and expansion of Comer Children's Hospital, including a paediatric emergency department and mobile care for pupils at local schools.
long_biography.html:
Gary Campbell Comer, the founder of Lands' End, learned to sail after joining a Chicago Park District boat-shop programme. Local sailors taught him in exchange for sanding and scrubbing their boats. He later won North American Star Class championships and a Pan American Games bronze medal. A Northwest Passage journey prompted him to investigate climate change; he funded fellowships for scientists studying abrupt shifts in the climate.

Comer directed substantial support towards the South Side neighbourhood where he grew up. His gifts helped establish the Gary Comer Youth Center beside his former elementary school. With his wife Frances, he supported the creation and expansion of Comer Children's Hospital, including a paediatric emergency department and mobile care for pupils at local schools.
